verdicts.evidence: The architecture spec was transcribed and found internally consistent, but the dLIF/ERG prior modules are explicitly 'specified but not yet coded'; only the encoder and classifier path is implemented, so the combined architecture was never exercised.

thm41_audit.py computed the event-prior KL two independent ways (direct integral vs change-of-variables Eq 9) with abs diff ≤1e-13 across three configurations, and controls showed both hypotheses (r bounded away from 0; Z_S normalization) are load-bearing.

On the toy dataset, reproduced latent-rate estimates match LERD's reported medians within 2–3.4% and a trajectory-only neural-ODE baseline scores IoU ~0 at CS ~0.99, but LERD's own IoU magnitudes (0.202–0.473) were not regenerated because they require the trained model.

A faithful pipeline was built and smoke-tested (1 fold, 3/30 epochs, 63.16% accuracy on CPU), but the full 5-fold × 30-epoch run was not executed and the dLIF/ERG priors were not coded, so the claimed 75.03% accuracy was never evaluated.
Cohort B (Sadegh-Zadeh et al., 2023) has Data Availability 'Not applicable' and no public mirror was found; the underlying EEG is private, so no experiments could be run.

The ablation numbers (Table 3) were not generated (GPU-bound, full model not trained), and LERD-inferred dLIF frequencies (Figure 2) were not reproduced; only the raw-EEG spectral-slowing premise was verified on 88 subjects (AD centroid below HC in 19/19 channels), which is a proxy for the model-derived claim.

overall: The logbook provides concrete numerical verification of Theorem 4.1's KL-surrogate identity and partial reproduction of the toy benchmark's baseline-failure and rate-recovery aspects, plus a raw-EEG check of the AD spectral-slowing premise on 88 real subjects. However, the paper's central empirical claims—Cohort A/B classification accuracy, ablation contributions, and model-derived IoU and dLIF frequencies—were not reproduced due to compute constraints, unimplemented modules, and unavailable data.
